speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a recent low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; have you noticed any specific pattern to the rash or if it appeared suddenly after being around sick contacts?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The timeline you described—a one-week prodrome of fever, rhinorrhea, and headache followed by a pruritic rash that spares the perioral area—is highly characteristic of a specific viral illness. Given her age and these specific symptoms, is there a possibility she has been exposed to anyone with a similar "slapped cheek" facial rash recently? REQUEST IMAGES: If you can provide any images of the facial rash, that would be very helpful.
